title: Day 1 antonio_calm. Follow to be next!
originalTitle: Day 1 antonio_calm. Follow to be next! #chess #chessimprovement #chessgame
reviewNotes: All 72 saved states and narration reviewed. London-game advice centers on an overloaded queen defending the backward e-pawn, Rh7?, exchanges on h7 and a middlegame king hunt ending in mate. The outside-passer/endgame references are hypothetical advice and the closing recommendation is to study endgames; neither supplies a worked endgame conversion. Many major/minor pieces and pawns remain in the illustrated finish. Retained as a searchable game review outside endgame-study scope.

So you're definitely on an upward trajectory and you should be higher rated pretty soon. And that makes sense because you, my friend, are a London player. So what I noticed is that you have already a pretty good grasp of this opening, first of all. The only thing that I would suggest, as a London player myself, is that when black is not allowed to push the C pawn, you want to do that yourself. Now you're basically putting some pressure in the black center right away. But what you've done also makes sense. Now whenever this black bishop is on our side of the board like this, we have ideas of attacking it with G4. And for example here, you could have won material right away with a knight to E5. If black captures, after we take back with the pawn, we're going to pick up the pawn here in the center. So that's a little idea you can keep in mind for the future. Instead you develop the bishop, that's still good. I like it and now you go with G4. Now here you could consider taking with the knight, that's what the engine wants as well. But I like what you did. You took with the queen. You castle, a lot of very good moves. You go F4, beautiful exploiting the fact that you have a pawn mass on this side of the board. You're opening things up. You keep pushing your pawns. But now after black takes, you take with the H pawn, which is fine. You had taken with the F pawn. Now in the future you always have the idea of creating an outside passer, which is a good thing to have in your pocket for the end game. And here is where everything goes south. You play rook to H7. Unfortunately, this is a pretty significant blunder. You are relying on the fact that the rook is defended by the queen. But whenever a piece is only defended by one other piece, you need to ask yourself, is that piece doing something where it is right now? Was that queen useful where it was? And the answer is yes. The queen is defending the very fundamental backwards e-pawn. And so, after black trades, you're going to lose that pawn, and all of a sudden you're already completely lost. You're going to lose some more material, and you do. And unfortunately, from here, your opponent plays very well. They pick up three pawns in just a few moves, and they continue with the initiative, and eventually you get checkmated like this. So, overall, I think you are definitely doing very well for your rating. Uh it's a shame for this one move. Uh and I would imagine that this is kind of like the tendency because I've seen that you're winning a lot of games, and that must mean that you have a pretty high level of understanding of positional chess and strategy and these kind of things, but you have a little bit of a skill issue when it comes to calculation. So, for you, my suggestion is to focus a little bit more on tactics, possibly do some puzzles, and to look a bit more at endgames and late middle games. Because it seems like you are playing the opening phase very well.
